the proteome and metabolome analyses of halophytes have been carried out to identify the salt responsive proteins and metabolites which are responsible for salinity tolerance.
halophytes can be a source of genes and gene products that are involved in the salt stress responses.
halophytes have developed several strategies to cope with the high salt concentration, including the synthesis of osmoprotectant and ion homeostasis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of salt tolerant genes and proteins in halophytes which could provide a basis for understanding the molecular mechanisms of salt tolerance.
the identification of salt tolerant genes in halophytes and their functional characterization for the development of salinity tolerance mechanism.
the elucidation of molecular mechanisms that underlie the adaptation of halophytes and glycophytes to salinity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the halophyte plants have a great capacity to adapt to the salt stress, and this capacity is due to a complex network of physiological, metabolic and proteomic processes.
the salt tolerance of halophytic plants is a complex process, and the mechanisms of salinity tolerance are not yet fully understood.

salinity tolerance mechanisms of halophyte species are not only dependent on their ability to maintain ionic and water balance, but also on the ability of their photosynthesis, red-ox homeostasis, stress response, carbohydrate and energy, protein and nucleic acid metabolisms, signal transduction, and membrane transport.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
salinity tolerance in plants is a highly complex phenomenon, which depends on the effective coordination of physiological processes and metabolic pathways.
the salinity responsive proteins, metabolites, and ionomic changes in halophytes would help in developing salt tolerant crops.
halophytes are the potential source of salt tolerance traits for crop improvement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
salinity tolerance in plants is a complex process that involves the coordinated regulation of a large number of genes, proteins and metabolites.

the salinity tolerance mechanisms of halophytic and glycophytic plants differ in terms of their proteomic, metabolomics and ionomics responses, and that these differences can be utilized to improve the salt tolerance of crops through transgenesis and/or breeding strategies.
halophytes can be used for understanding the mechanisms of salinity tolerance, which in turn can be used for improving the salt tolerance of glycophytes.
